name: Stalker AI
description: A relentless pursuer built on three rules: it always knows roughly where you are, it never moves faster than dread allows, and it announces itself before it arrives. Pathing is movement.pathfinding_system's; the stalker's contribution is offscreen telegraphing — audio stingers, lighting dips — driven by distance bands, because an unstoppable threat that arrives silently reads as unfair rather than frightening. It loses the trail through world.hiding_spot state and broken line of sight, never through a stealth stat, so hiding works because the fiction says the locker works. Noise pulls it: gunfire and loud movement are evidence, which is why the horror game's shotgun is also a dinner bell. What happens on catch is combat.damage_resolver's business or the setpiece script's — this component's job ends at contact.

inputs.name: patrolSpeed
inputs.description: Search speed while no trail is hot. Slower than the player's walk on purpose: the stalker's menace comes from persistence and knowledge, not from winning a footrace.

inputs.name: pursuitSpeed
inputs.description: Speed with a live trail. Tuned just under the player's sprint so escape is possible but expensive — a pursuer you can out-walk is weather, not a threat.

inputs.name: loseTrailSeconds
inputs.description: How long after losing sight and sound the pursuit state persists. Short enough that breaking contact works; long enough that rounding one corner never saves you.

inputs.name: telegraphDistanceBands
inputs.description: Distances at which escalating telegraphs fire (distant audio, near audio, lighting dip). Bands are crossed in both directions, so the relief of it moving AWAY is also communicated — dread needs contrast to work.

inputs.name: lastKnownMemorySeconds
inputs.description: How long the stalker searches around the last known position before reverting to patrol. The search is a slow spiral, not a camp — a stalker that parks on your last position turns hiding into waiting.

outputs.name: currentState
outputs.description: patrol, search, or pursuit — the utility.behavior_fsm state name, exposed so audio and lighting can stage the telegraph bands against actual intent.

outputs.name: distanceToTarget
outputs.description: Live distance to the hunted entity. Telegraphs key off this, not off vision state, because the scariest band is the one where IT knows and YOU don't.

outputs.name: isOffscreen
outputs.description: True while the stalker is outside every player view. Telegraph events only fire offscreen — a monster you can see needs no announcer.
